title: Resources and Asynchronous State knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Resources and Asynchronous State”?
options: Resources and Asynchronous State helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
Resources and Asynchronous State means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Resources and Asynchronous State removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Resources and Asynchronous State should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
questions.answer_key: Resources and Asynchronous State helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Resources and Asynchronous State is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “The resource() API” in this lesson?
options: Treat “The resource() API” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
Assume “The resource() API” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “The resource() API” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “The resource() API” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.answer_key: Connect “The resource() API” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “The resource() API” under Resources and Asynchronous State. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Resources and Asynchronous State”?
options: Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
